newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds and futures look to U.S. data for signal.
newsitem.headline: Bunds and futures look to U.S. data for signal.

text.p: German Bunds and futures are likely to remian close to base in the first half of Thursday's session, awaiting two key economic releases from the U.S.
Analysts say the long end of the market in particular will be driven by movements in Treasuries, while the short end will continue to focus more on domestic issues.
Second quarter U.S. GDP data, due at 1230 GMT, are expected to show a substantial slowing in economic growth to around 1.9 percent from 5.9 percent in the first quarter.
If the figures come in line with expectations, a relief rally in Treasuries will support German debt, analysts said.
"The U.S. GDP. price index and Chicago PMI have market moving potential," MMS analysts said in a morning note.
But they said shorter-dated German paper would remain more sensitive to domestic conerns about the weaknes of the mark and the potential risk of a repo rate move by the Bundesbank.

"The Bundesbank will probably be more concerned with the rate of any deutschemark fall, rather than the levels per se. Any signals of a sinificant shift in market sentiment on this score could see rate hike expectations brought forward."
Two and three-year paper was particularly vulnerable on this issue, MMS said.
By 0652 GMT the September DTB Bund future was trading one basis point lower on the day, shedding the gains it made just after the open when it hit an early high of 103.42.
Traders said the contract was not likely to go far before the U.S. data, but could be sparked into action later.

"If we get confirmation of the slowdown in the U.S. economy there's a chance the futures could take out the 103.58 high," said one Frankfurt-based trader. The September future plotted a contract high at this level on July 23.
On the downside, traders said losses should be limited to 103.00.

In the cash market, the 10-year benchmark Bund was quoted one tick higher at 103.72 for a bid yield of 5.494 percent, while the short end continued to remain under pressure, trading mostly lower on the day.
